info.bio: Bon Jovi es una banda estadounidense de Hard Rock que alcanzó la fama mundial gracias a los éxitos internacionales: "Livin' On A Prayer", "You Give Love A Bad Name", "Bad Medicine" y "I'll Be There For You", a mediados de los 80's; Fue formada en New Jersey, en 1983 por Jon Bon Jovi (su verdadero nombre es John Francis Bongiovi). Con Richie Sambora en la guitarra, David Bryan en los teclados, Tico Torres (Hector Torres) como bateria y Alec John Such como bajista (sustituido en 1995 por Hugh McDonald)

scenes.name: Lite metal: pop metal y glam
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: El subgénero que, desde 1983-84, intensifica el polo melódico del heavy y lo mezcla con el hard rock, quitándole el grave grueso. Philip Bashe lo llamó «metal pop» y señaló a Def Leppard y Van Halen; otros ejemplos son Poison, Bon Jovi, Ratt y Cinderella. Sus detractores, el público tradicional y el del thrash, lo llaman «poseurs», «false metal», «nerf metal», «poodle bands» o «glam», motes que describen bien sus rasgos: falta de autenticidad, pelo cardado, ropa colorida en lugar del negro obrero. Voz dulce sin gruñidos, armonías al modo de Aerosmith y Kiss, letras de amor y lujuria con nombres de chica y, sobre todo, la power ballad, que entra en radios que excluían el heavy y gana público nuevo, como las versiones blancas de Pat Boone en los cincuenta. MTV impulsó mucho su desarrollo. Se queda con la herencia dionisíaca y elimina el caos: «lo realmente pesado se quita».

scenes.name: MTV y Headbangers Ball
scenes.book: Heavy Metal: The Music and Its Culture
scenes.author: Deena Weinstein
scenes.desc: MTV nace en agosto de 1981 y en dos años casi monopoliza el videoclip. El heavy, visual desde que Judas Priest se vistió de cuero, es un candidato natural: entre los primeros grupos emitidos están Quiet Riot, Mötley Crüe, Twisted Sister, Dokken y Scorpions, y la cuota de mercado del metal salta del 8 % en 1983 al 20 % en 1984 («MTV fue responsable del resurgir del heavy», dice Dee Snider). A principios de 1985 la presión fundamentalista lo recorta, pero en 1988 nace el programa nocturno «Headbangers Ball». MTV selecciona del metal lo compatible con un público juvenil general: hace del lite metal un coautor del género (pelo cardado, chico malo mono, chicas en el público) y empuja al thrash, casi ausente, a definirse como antítesis comercial. Los vídeos, rodados por directores de publicidad, cuestan cada vez más (190.000 dólares uno de Poison en 1989) y dejan fuera a las bandas pequeñas, convierten los conciertos en simulacros del vídeo y, al llevar el metal al salón familiar, despiertan a sus enemigos: la lista de los «Filthy Fifteen» del PMRC y el departamento de normas de MTV.

scenes.name: La edad de oro del heavy metal
scenes.author: Piero Scaruffi
scenes.desc: El heavy metal renace en los mismos años que la new wave, aprovechando los sellos independientes: Motörhead (puente entre metal, Stooges/MC5 y punk), Judas Priest, Iron Maiden, Diamond Head, Def Leppard y, en EE UU, Van Halen. Entre 1982 y 1985 el subgénero gótico se convierte en «black metal» (Venom, Mercyful Fate, Celtic Frost, Helloween, Bathory). El pop-metal y el shock-rock (Twisted Sister, Mötley Crüe, Joan Jett, Bon Jovi, Savatage); la pompa y el doom (Manowar, Voivod, Saint Vitus, Pentagram); el metal progresivo (Living Colour, Queensrÿche, King's X, Pantera, Joe Satriani) y el «street sound» de Los Ángeles (Guns N' Roses, Jane's Addiction, Faster Pussycat).

mentions.text: …However, American heavy-metal of the 1980s remained mainly a "pop-metal crossover", a genre that would peak in the mid 1980s with New Jersey's Bon Jovi, led by melodramatic shouter Jon Bongiovi and acrobatic guitarist Richie Sambora, a band that coined a magniloquent style with You Give Love A Bad…

podcast.title: Ascendant American Rock Band
podcast.body: Bon Jovi replaced The Human League at number one on the Hot 100 one week after "Human" topped the charts in late 1986, signaling their ascendancy and the end of the second British invasion. "One week after human topped the Hot 100, the human league were replaced at number one by this band of vulgar Americans. Bon Jovi were ascendant, American Anglo-Files had been put in their place, and the second British invasion was over."

podcast.title: Audience Rejection and Sound Evolution
podcast.body: In their early days, while opening for the German heavy metal band The Scorpions, Bon Jovi's "poppy sound" was met with disdain by some fans, who responded by throwing coins at the band and shouting, "get the fuck off the stage." Despite this initial rejection, Bon Jovi forged ahead, borrowing from Van Halen's approach to make hard rock fun with singalong choruses, and notably embraced synthesizers, an instrument previously associated with disco. "The fans responded to this poppy sound by throwing coins at the guys in the band as and get the fuck off the stage."

podcast.title: Early Career Ambitions and Influences
podcast.body: While still a high school student, New Jersey native John Bon Jovi was actively forming a rock band and performing in local clubs. He recalled the surreal experience of sharing a microphone on stage with "the biggest rock star in New Jersey" (implying Bruce Springsteen) at 17, envisioning a future filled with "rainbows and unicorns" after this encounter. "I'm a 17 year old kid and suddenly I'm sharing a microphone on stage with the biggest rock star in New Jersey."

podcast.title: Early Glam Metal Identity
podcast.body: In 1984, Bon Jovi was considered a metal band, emblematic of the glam metal style. The term "hair metal" was only coined a couple of years later, after they began topping the Hot 100, distinguishing their sound from other metal subgenres. "They really were considered metal at that time. After they began topping the Hot 100 a couple of years later, the term hair metal was coined."

podcast.title: Post-Hair Metal Career Shift
podcast.body: While Bon Jovi continued to achieve success in the 1990s, it never quite matched the "sweet spot of the hair metal era." Recognizing this, the band made a conscious decision to move away from their hair metal image towards "more 'serious' rock music," a strategic move that was considered wise as the hair metal era abruptly concluded. "Bonjouvi would continue to have success in the 90s but it was never quite like the sweet spot of the hair metal era and looking back on it, I think they were wise to move away from that image to more air quotes serious rock music because the hair metal era ended about as abruptly as it started."

podcast.title: Session Musicians for Debut Single
podcast.body: For their debut single, "Runaway," John Bon Jovi fronted a group of "journeyman session musicians" with whom he never played again. This marked a unique point in the band's history, as the lineup was not yet fully solidified for their initial chart success. "On it, John Bon Jovi, fronted a group of journeyman session musicians he never played with again."

xref.title: Founding and Location (1977)
xref.body: The Power Station, located in New York at approximately 53rd and 10th, was founded in 1977 by Tony Bongiovi, the second cousin of John Bon Jovi. The building previously served as a Consolidated Edison power plant and later a TV studio for "Let's Make a Deal." "In 1977, the building was bought and rebuilt as a recording studio by Tony Bongeovi, the second cousin of some New Jersey kid named John Bongeovi."

xref.title: Battle of Bands Win Led to Bob Rock's First Ever Production Credit
xref.body: The band started as the K-Tels in 1978 in Vancouver but were threatened with legal action by the cheap record company K-tel International and renamed themselves Young Canadians. Frontman Art Bergman would remain a presence in Canadian alt-rock for decades, ultimately being made a Member of the Order of Canada in 2020. The band won a local Battle of the Bands contest that awarded them studio time at a new facility called Little Mountain Sound. The engineer assigned to these unknown contest winners was a young man named Bob Rock — it was the first time Rock ever produced anything. He went on to produce Metallica, Mötley Crüe, Bon Jovi, The Cult, the Tragically Hip, and many others. "The engineer assigned to them was some kid named Bob Rock."

xref.body: Throughout the 1980s and 1990s, Fairbairn produced mega-platinum albums for numerous major rock bands, including Aerosmith, AC/DC, Bon Jovi, INXS, Kiss, Loverboy, Poison, The Scorpions, and Van Halen, accumulating close to 100 million album sales. xref.title: High-Profile Tours and Collaborations
xref.body: Orianthi served as the guitarist in Carrie Underwood's band and was slated to be Michael Jackson's lead guitarist for his final planned tour. Her extensive collaborative work includes performances with Richie Sambora (Bon Jovi), Hollywood Vampires, Don Felder (The Eagles), and Michael Bolton, as well as recording with Dave Stewart. "She ended up as the guitarist and carry Underwood's band and had Michael Jackson lived to tour one more time Orienthi was going to be in his band as lead guitarist."
